```{r setup, include = FALSE}
can_eval <- requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("duckplyr", quietly = TRUE) &&
  reactableduckdb:::has_reactable_backend_api()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = can_eval
)
```

reactableduckdb streams a lazy DuckDB query — a duckplyr data frame or a
dbplyr lazy table — into a [reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/)
widget through reactable's custom server-side data backend API. DuckDB
performs **all** filtering, counting, sorting, and pagination.

Only three things are ever materialized into R:

1. a **zero-row schema prototype** (once, at backend construction),
2. a **scalar filtered count** (one number per distinct filter state), and
3. the **requested page of rows** (bounded by `max_page_size`).

Nothing else is collected — the complete source dataset never enters R.
Anything the backend cannot do honestly it **refuses loudly** (a structured
error) instead of silently falling back to eager execution or returning
wrong data.

> **Dependency note**: this package requires the **development version** of
> reactable (>= 0.4.5.9000), which exports the server backend API; the CRAN
> release does not. Install it from GitHub (`pak::pak("glin/reactable")`),
> or from a Posit Package Manager repository that mirrors that GitHub
> repository and needs no GitHub access. Either route
> works — reactableduckdb declares no `Remotes` and does not require a
> particular one. If the API is missing, the package warns once naming both
> routes rather than refusing to load.

## The intended workflow

The application owns its pins and its data pipeline; the package only
exposes the lazy result:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pin_path <- pins::pin_download(board, "example-data")

source_data <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(pin_path, prudence = "stingy") |>
  dplyr::filter(distance_mi > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(delay_hr = delay_min / 60) |>
  dplyr::select(flight_id, carrier, distance_mi, delay_hr)

backend <- reactable_duckdb_backend(source_data, key = "flight_id")

# In a Shiny server:
output$flights <- reactable::renderReactable(
  reactable_duckdb(backend, filterable = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 50L)
)
```

A working self-contained app ships with the package:
`system.file("examples", "app.R", package = "reactableduckdb")`.

```{r echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, out.width = "100%", fig.alt = "The example Shiny app: a reactable table of 100,000 flights with the numeric range filter >=1500 applied to the distance column, showing 49,500 filtered rows paginated across 990 pages. Every column has a filter box except the display-only LIST column."}
knitr::include_graphics("../man/figures/example-app.png")
```

*The screenshot is captured manually from the example app and may lag the
current UI; regeneration steps are in the header of `inst/examples/app.R`.*

### `group_by()` does not work under `prudence = "stingy"` — use `.by`

duckplyr refuses `group_by()` on a stingy source. Use the `.by` argument
instead; it stays fully lazy:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Errors under prudence = "stingy":
source_data |> dplyr::group_by(carrier) |> dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n())

# Works, stays lazy:
source_data |> dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), .by = carrier)
```

## What one request executes

```{r}
library(reactableduckdb)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE TABLE flights AS
  SELECT i AS id, 'CARRIER_' || (i % 12) AS carrier,
         (i % 3000)::INTEGER AS distance
  FROM range(100000) r(i)")

backend <- reactable_duckdb_backend(dplyr::tbl(con, "flights"), key = "id")
reactableduckdb:::enable_query_log(backend)

page <- reactable::reactableServerData(
  backend,
  pageIndex = 2,
  pageSize = 5,
  sortBy = list(list(id = "distance", desc = TRUE)),
  filters = list(list(id = "carrier", value = "carrier_3"))
)
page$rowCount
page$data
```

Two queries ran — a scalar count and a bounded page — and nothing else:

```{r}
cat(paste(backend$state$query_log, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

Note the shape: the user's filter value is a **bound literal** inside the
dbplyr-rendered subquery (never pasted into SQL), ordering is explicit
`NULLS LAST` in both directions with the `key` appended as a deterministic
tie-breaker, and pagination is integer-only `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`.

## Filtering

The full grammar lives in `design/filter-contract.md`; the short version:

| Column type | Grammar |
| --- | --- |
| text | case-insensitive literal substring; `%`, `_`, quotes all literal; `filter_spec` can force `exact` |
| numeric | `10`, `-5`, `1.5`, `1e6`, `>=10`, `<-5`, `10..20` |
| date | `2026-01-01`, `>=2026-01-01`, `2026-01-01..2026-01-31` |
| datetime | ISO, interpreted as UTC instants, same comparators/ranges |
| logical | `true/false/t/f/1/0`, case-insensitive |
| LIST/STRUCT/MAP/BLOB | **display-only**: rendered, never filterable or sortable |

Malformed input (e.g. `abc` in a numeric column, `2026-02-30`) raises a
structured package error, never a raw database error. Empty input means no
filter. Missing-value filtering is deferred in v1: NULL rows never match a
filter, and sorting places NULLs last in both directions.

## Refusals

Unsupported features error at widget construction rather than degrading:
`server`, `data`, `searchable = TRUE`, `searchMethod`, `groupBy`,
`pagination = FALSE`, `paginateSubRows = TRUE`, `rownames = TRUE`, a
`defaultPageSize` or `pageSizeOptions` entry above `max_page_size`, and
explicitly re-enabling filter/sort on a display-only column. `selection`
and `details` are allowed but apply to the **current page only**.

Oversized page requests at runtime are refused, never clamped. In a live
Shiny app a refused request surfaces as a failed (HTTP 500) data request
and the table keeps its previous rows; the app's log carries a structured
line with the backend's schema hash and the offending column ids (never
filter values). Debounce filter inputs in production — reactable fires a
request per keystroke.

## Backend lifecycle, cache, and keys

- The filtered **count is cached** (bounded LRU) per canonical filter set:
  paging and re-sorting reuse it; changing filters does not. An app-global
  backend over an immutable source shares its cache across sessions.
- A live backend **cannot detect** that its source, schema, or pin changed,
  and never reconnects or refreshes. When the source changes, construct a
  new backend and re-render. An invalid connection errors with exactly that
  instruction.
- `key` should be a **unique** orderable column; it makes page order
  deterministic. Uniqueness is the caller's responsibility unless you opt
  into `validate_key = TRUE` (one scalar scan at construction).
- Very deep `OFFSET` pagination is increasingly expensive in any SQL
  engine; cursor pagination is out of scope for v1.

Outside a Shiny session the widget renders empty (only the zero-row
prototype is embedded) — the server backend needs a live session.

```{r, include = FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```
